steps.tx: Chemotherapy-induced suppression of bone marrow haematopoiesis represents an acute oncological emergency predisposed to rapid fatal septicaemia. **Febrile neutropenia** is an oncologic emergency defined as oral temperature 38.3 deg C or higher once or 38.0 deg C sustained for 1 hour with absolute neutrophil count **ANC under 500/mcL** or expected to fall under 500/mcL within 48 hours. Rapid bacterial invasion occurs across damaged mucosal barriers without local inflammatory signs.

nodes.label: Oral Temperature >= 38.3 deg C (or >= 38.0 for 1 hr)
Loss of Normal Inflammatory Pus Formation
Rapid Translocation of Endogenous Mucosal Flora
Mandatory Empiric Broad-Spectrum IV Antibiotics in < 1 hr

edges: Golden hour resuscitation prevents septic shock

steps.tx: The Multinational Association for Supportive Care in Cancer **MASCC index** identifies **low-risk febrile** neutropenia eligible for outpatient oral antibiotic therapy with a score of 21 or higher. A score of 21 or higher indicates a low risk of serious medical complications, permitting outpatient oral therapy with ciprofloxacin plus amoxicillin-clavulanate in reliable patients with close monitoring.

left.title: MASCC Score >= 21 (Low Risk)
points: Low risk of severe medical complications (< 5%)
Eligible for outpatient care after 4 hours of observation
Daily telephone follow-up and 24-hour return precautions

right.title: MASCC Score < 21 (High Risk)
points: High risk of complications (septic shock, ICU transfer, death)
Mandatory inpatient admission for intravenous antibiotics
Inpatient monitoring for anticipated neutropenia duration > 7 days
Associated with severe comorbidities or haematologic malignancy

steps.tx: The Clinical Index of Stable Febrile Neutropenia **CISNE score** specifically stratifies **solid tumour** patients presenting with febrile neutropenia to identify candidates for outpatient care. The CISNE scoring model excludes unstable patients, utilizing performance status, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, cardiovascular disease, stress-induced hyperglycaemia, and mucositis to identify genuinely low-risk outpatients.

rows: Carbapenem of choice for ESBL risk or septic shock
Add for MRSA risk, central line sepsis, or severe mucositis

steps.tx: High-risk febrile neutropenia mandates immediate inpatient empirical monotherapy with an **antipseudomonal beta-lactam** such as **piperacillin-tazobactam**, cefepime, or meropenem within 1 hour of presentation. Delay in antimicrobial administration beyond 60 minutes significantly elevates 28-day mortality from Gram-negative sepsis, particularly Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteraemia.

rows: Fixed 6 mg SC single dose per chemotherapy cycle
Administer strictly 24 hours post-chemo; avoids daily injections
Indicated after prior cycle febrile neutropenia
Maintains full planned dose intensity and schedule
Manage with NSAIDs or loratadine antihistamine

steps.tx: **Primary prophylaxis** with **granulocyte colony-stimulating** factors G-CSF filgrastim or pegfilgrastim is recommended when the anticipated regimen risk of febrile neutropenia is 20% or higher. Prophylactic myeloid growth factor support reduces the incidence of febrile neutropenia, shortens hospitalization, and maintains planned chemotherapy dose intensity across curative-intent regimens.

nodes.label: Persistent Neutropenic Fever at Day 4 to 7
Assess Mould vs Yeast Risk Factors
Initiate Caspofungin or Liposomal Amphotericin B
Voriconazole if Pulmonary Halo Sign Identified

edges: Diagnostic workup for invasive fungal disease

steps.tx: Prolonged remission induction in acute leukaemias creates sustained profound neutropenia requiring mold-active prophylaxis. **Posaconazole prophylaxis** significantly reduces proven or probable **invasive aspergillosis** and all-cause mortality in neutropenic patients undergoing remission induction for AML or MDS. In a pivotal randomized trial, posaconazole delayed-release tablets or oral suspension demonstrated superior fungal prophylaxis compared to fluconazole or itraconazole.

left.title: Posaconazole Prophylaxis (Delayed-Release)
points: Broad mold coverage including Aspergillus and Mucorales
Statistically significant reduction in all-cause mortality (p=0.04)
Mandated standard in AML/MDS intensive induction chemotherapy

right.title: Fluconazole Prophylaxis
points: 400 mg daily oral or intravenous administration
Active only against Candida species (lacks Aspergillus activity)
Ineffective in preventing invasive mould infections
Reserved for low-risk solid tumour or autologous transplant settings

steps.tx: Growth factors stimulating erythrocyte production carry oncological risks requiring strict restriction to palliative settings. **Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents** ESAs are indicated only for palliative **chemotherapy-induced anaemia** with haemoglobin under 10 g/dL, avoiding use when cure is the anticipated outcome. Meta-analyses demonstrated that ESAs stimulate erythropoietin receptors on tumour cells, shortening overall survival and increasing thromboembolic vascular events in curative-intent cancer regimens.

rows: Haemoglobin < 10 g/dL during active palliative chemo
Do not administer if chemotherapy has ended
Maintain lowest Hb level needed to avoid transfusion (<= 10-12 g/dL)
Targeting Hb > 12 g/dL increases stroke and mortality
Strictly contra-indicated in curative-intent breast, lung, HNSCC
Assess baseline thrombosis risk prior to initiation

steps.tx: Prophylactic platelet transfusions prevent fatal spontaneous haemorrhage during chemotherapy-induced marrow hypoplasia. **Platelet transfusions** are indicated prophylactically at a threshold of **10 x 10^9/L or lower** in stable **hypoproliferative thrombocytopenia**, and at 20 x 10^9/L in the presence of fever or bleeding. A single apheresis platelet unit or pooled random donor platelets provides approximately 30,000 to 50,000/mcL platelet increment, preventing spontaneous microvascular bleeding.
